A_target.statement:
Let $V$ be a [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] $K$.
Then the [[Definition:Exterior Algebra|exterior algebra]] of $V$ is:
:$\map \Lambda V = \map T V / \ideal {v \otimes v: v \in V}$
where $\map T V$ is the [[Definition:Tensor Algebra|tensor algebra]].

B_source.statement:
Let $f: A \to B$ be an [[Definition:Algebra Homomorphism|algebra homomorphism]].
Then:
:$A / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$

substitutions.the ideal of relations: the two-sided ideal generated by elements v tensor v

derived.the universal property: every alternating multilinear map factors uniquely through Lambda(V)

validity_conditions: the ideal must be two-sided for the quotient to be an algebra
generating by v tensor v rather than by v tensor w + w tensor v is required in characteristic two, where the two conditions differ
the grading survives the quotient because the ideal is generated by homogeneous elements
proof_plan: Start from $\map T V$, the [[Definition:Free Algebra|free]] [[Definition:Associative Algebra|associative algebra]] on $V$.
[[Definition:Alternating Mapping|Alternation]] forces every $v \otimes v$ to vanish.

Let $I = \ideal {v \otimes v: v \in V}$ be the two-sided [[Definition:Ideal of Algebra|ideal]] they generate.
Each generator lies in $V^{\otimes 2}$, so $I$ is [[Definition:Homogeneous Ideal|homogeneous]].
By the isomorphism-theorem pattern, algebra maps $\map T V / I \to A$ correspond to algebra maps $\map T V \to A$ killing $I$, that is, linear maps $\phi: V \to A$ with $\map \phi v^2 = 0$.
